scope.purpose: Select physical quality experiments from observed defects. This resource does not score or guarantee finish, fit or strength.
scope.materials: FFF materials within the confirmed machine, nozzle, plate and material specifications. PETG evidence is conditional on its stated formulation and setup.
limits: Read current catalog types and scopes before each edit.
Other slicers' documentation explains mechanisms. It does not establish feature parity with this Studio version.
No source supplies a universal speed, temperature, fan percentage, K value or dimensional offset.
External experiments do not validate this user's printer, spool or geometry.

guidance: Confirm the actual firmware, plate, enclosure, every nozzle variant and each spool's feeding path.
Check exact printer, nozzle, filament and accessory documentation before using a profile.
Distinguish automatic feeding from a dryer used with its feeder bypassed.
A hotend component rating does not raise the printer's supported temperature limit.
Preserve unresolved source conflicts. Do not bypass compatibility restrictions by changing a profile label.
scope_limits: These checks require physical setup declarations and current external documentation.
capability_limits: The server does not query printer firmware or verify installed accessories.
Firmware and Studio versions can change accessory and nozzle support.
A family name or material abbreviation alone does not prove compatibility.
acceptance_checks: Record exact hardware and material products, document URLs and relevant version requirements.
Resolve unsupported or conflicting combinations before a physical trial.

guidance: Keep manufacturer limits, measured experiments and community anecdotes distinct.
Record an experiment's printer, nozzle, filament formulation and color, orientation, temperature, flow and specimen before transferring its method.
Use maximum volumetric flow as an extrusion limit, not a surface-finish or strength certificate.
Do not use a higher flow ratio to compensate for an extrusion system beyond its melting capacity.
Treat changes of formulation, finish, color or nozzle as reasons to review relevant calibration and physical acceptance.
scope_limits: External experiments justify a candidate method. Their numeric results are not defaults for another setup.
capability_limits: Filament indexes, physical extruders, nozzle variants and AMS slots are different mappings.
The server leaves ambiguous calibration-vector comparisons unknown.
acceptance_checks: Compare a matched baseline and candidate using the actual material and critical geometry.
Record fit, finish and strength separately. A better appearance does not prove greater strength.

guidance: Confirm the printer, nozzle diameter and material, plate, exact filament product and color.
Identify the defective surface and its intended use.
Keep unknown properties explicit. A saved filament profile does not identify the actual spool.
Use exact manufacturer limits. Use a compatible Generic profile as an unverified baseline when exact specifications remain unknown.
capability_limits: The server cannot identify a physical spool or inspect an unsaved GUI project.
acceptance_checks: Record the actual spool and installed nozzle.
Separate manufacturer specifications, profile defaults and measured calibration.

guidance: Check dryness, nozzle condition and extrusion faults before calibration.
Use the exact manufacturer's procedure for filament drying.
Keep temperature, maximum volumetric flow, flow dynamics K and flow ratio separate.
An example calibration sequence is temperature, maximum volumetric flow, pressure advance, flow ratio, then retraction.
Repeat affected calibration after temperature, throughput, nozzle or filament changes.
scope_limits: Nozzle temperature keys are project-only in this catalog. Filament flow ratio and maximum volumetric speed also allow filament scope.
capability_limits: The server cannot measure moisture, perform physical calibration or confirm a printer-side K value.
The PETG drying experiment used a different filament and printer. Its recipe and effect size do not transfer automatically.
For P1S, use Bambu's manual flow dynamics procedure. Other printer models require their supported procedure.
Generic enable_pressure_advance and pressure_advance fields do not implement Bambu printer K calibration.
acceptance_checks: Record the procedure, nozzle, filament, temperature and physical result.
Check a representative sample after calibration. Do not equate an accepted slice with calibration.

guidance: Compare temperature within the exact material and nozzle limits.
Recheck temperature after a substantial flow or speed change.
Higher cooling can improve bridges and overhangs. Excessive cooling can weaken layer bonds or increase warping.
Choose cooling from the observed surface and load requirements.
scope_limits: These temperature and fan keys are project-only in the pinned catalog.
capability_limits: Slow PETG can ooze at a temperature that works at higher flow.
A transparency recipe with fans off does not validate ordinary opaque parts or threads.
No universal fan percentage or temperature follows from material type alone.
acceptance_checks: Compare the affected underside, visible face and layer adhesion on the same specimen.
Keep the baseline and other calibration conditions explicit.

guidance: Inspect actual slice output before a physical trial.
Distinguish requested speed, emitted feed commands and actual attained speed.
Review Studio-normalized settings and warnings.
Separate purge and nozzle-cleanup temperature targets from first-layer and object-extrusion temperatures.
capability_limits: A cleanup temperature does not establish object print temperature.
Time and filament estimates do not measure surface quality, fit or strength.
A G-code command does not measure the nozzle's actual temperature or attained speed.
acceptance_checks: Check the temperature context at first object extrusion and later layers.
Confirm the intended layer heights, feature settings and effective toolpaths.

guidance: Use a small specimen with the same critical geometry, orientation, material and local process as the final part.
Compare an unchanged baseline with one deliberate change.
Define fit, surface or load criteria before the trial.
Keep physical outcomes unverified until the user supplies observations or measurements.
capability_limits: A plain hole does not validate a helical thread.
The server cannot crop specimens, generate thread CAD, measure surface roughness or certify loads.
acceptance_checks: Record the revision, setup, specimen geometry, criteria and observed result.
Use repeat samples for important decisions. Compare photographs under the same light.

categories.label: Threads and small features
observation_needed: Is the thread tight, loose, rough, damaged or difficult to start?
Identify the actual screw, thread geometry, engagement depth, axis and defect height.

guidance: Inspect the existing small-perimeter threshold before a speed change.
In the pinned implementation, the threshold is an equivalent radius: loop perimeter divided by 2*pi.
A zero threshold disables this slowdown for nonempty loops.
Select a nonzero threshold from the actual contour and compare a calibrated small-perimeter speed.
Percentage small-perimeter speed is relative to outer-wall speed.
scope_limits: These keys allow project, object, volume and height_range scopes. Preserve vector values.
Use a layer-height profile for regional layer resolution. layer_height itself is project-only.
capability_limits: Nominal thread diameter alone does not identify every affected contour.
Slower commanded speed does not guarantee better fit or finish.
The server does not automatically identify or create thread geometry.
acceptance_checks: Check emitted speeds on the intended thread contours and unchanged regions.
Print the same thread, boss and actual screw. Check start, engagement, binding, debris and repeated assembly.

guidance: Inspect the existing orientation and local layer profile before extra refinement.
Compare local layer resolution or orientation only when the thread geometry requires it.
Keep functional dimensions unchanged during a surface comparison.
scope_limits: Use edit_regions layer_heights within nozzle limits. A layer profile replaces the complete previous profile.
capability_limits: No fixed layers-per-pitch ratio proves thread quality.
Rotation can change support needs and other critical surfaces.
acceptance_checks: Check the actual layer profile through the entire thread.
Use a specimen with the same pitch, engagement and screw.

categories.label: Visible walls
observation_needed: Identify the cosmetic face and distinguish ripples, corner ringing, horizontal bands, sheen changes and extrusion defects.

guidance: Compare a speed or acceleration specimen after material calibration.
Inspect maximum-flow and cooling limits before a speed comparison.
Use speed smoothing for matching discontinuity defects. Read current settings first.
Slower speed is a candidate, not a universal improvement.
scope_limits: outer_wall_acceleration and z_direction_outwall_speed_continuous are project-only.
The other listed controls allow local scopes according to the catalog.
capability_limits: Z-direction smoothing targets continuous wall bands. Interrupted geometry can limit its benefit.
A commanded speed target does not prove actual speed or surface quality.
acceptance_checks: Check actual toolpaths and time cost.
Compare the same face under the same light. Check overhangs and dimensions separately.

guidance: Compare wall order only after the user identifies the target surface.
Inner-outer-inner requires at least three walls for its intended sequence.
Inspect the actual order around critical holes and narrow shared walls.
Compare precise outer wall only where adjacent wall deposition can distort the contour.
scope_limits: wall_sequence is project-only. Do not promise a height-range-only wall-order change.
capability_limits: Preferred order can fail on narrow or shared contours.
Outer-first behavior can reduce sharp-overhang support. Orca issue reports do not prove this Studio has the same defect.
acceptance_checks: Verify emitted order on the affected contours.
Compare hole fit, overhangs and visible walls on physical samples.

guidance: Compare the current orientation with an upright curve through edit_regions rotate.
Use this candidate for geometric stair steps on shallow curves, not every dull or matte surface.
Check support contact, bed stability, build height and load direction after rotation.
Compare local wall speed, temperature and cooling separately when gloss varies.
scope_limits: Read catalog scopes and the actual nozzle profile before an edit.
capability_limits: This procedure applies to P1S and other Bambu printers within their confirmed build envelopes.
Upright orientation can reduce visible steps on one face and worsen supports or strength elsewhere.
A brighter reflection does not prove a stronger part. No orientation guarantees gloss.
acceptance_checks: Compare the same curved face under the same light.
Compare slicer estimates, supports and physical stability against the baseline.

categories.label: Seams and travel marks
observation_needed: Locate seams relative to visible faces, functional holes and overhangs. Distinguish seam ridges from general roughness.

guidance: Compare seam placement or existing seam paint before a scarf experiment.
Random placement distributes seam marks. It does not remove them.
Keep seams away from critical fit surfaces where geometry permits.
scope_limits: These settings are project-only. Use existing seam paint for local face selection.
capability_limits: Paint affects every instance of the shared mesh resource.
Travel detours cost time and do not remove every crossing.
acceptance_checks: Inspect actual seam locations and travel paths.
Check the chosen visible face and screw engagement on a physical sample.

guidance: Compare conditional contour scarf as a separate experiment after flow calibration.
Check whether the filament or process setting controls scarf behavior.
Do not extend scarf to functional holes before a matched fit trial.

Check activation before tuning: zero scarf length can disable scarf unless entire-wall mode applies, and 100% start height becomes an ordinary seam. Smart scarf can intentionally skip corners or overhangs.
scope_limits: seam_slope_type is project-only. Filament scarf type allows filament scope.
A process scarf type does not override the filament unless the override is active.
capability_limits: Whole-loop scarf and low extrusion on overhangs can cause defects.
A PLA recipe from another slicer does not validate PETG thread settings.
acceptance_checks: Verify actual scarf paths and the controlling setting.
Compare seam appearance, adhesion and dimensions. Retain the ordinary seam baseline.

categories.label: Flat and curved top surfaces
observation_needed: Distinguish a flat top, rounded dome, vertical wall and supported underside before a remedy.

guidance: Read the current top pattern before a proposed change.
Retain a monotonic baseline when it already meets the surface goal.
Compare top flow or speed after extrusion calibration.
scope_limits: top_surface_pattern is project-only. Check the catalog before a local flow or speed edit.
capability_limits: Uniform top texture does not establish internal strength.
acceptance_checks: Inspect actual top paths.
Compare filled gaps, ridges, sheen and the effect on sharp edges.

guidance: Compare ironing only on an applicable horizontal top specimen.
Check flow, spacing and speed together through a bounded experiment.
For PETG, inspect nozzle deposits and dark particles during the physical trial.
scope_limits: ironing_type is project-only. Local parameter scopes do not provide local activation of ironing.
capability_limits: Ironing does not fix walls, slopes, threads or supported undersides.
Ironing adds time and can soften edges. PETG can stick to the nozzle.
acceptance_checks: Review every affected top surface before export.
Compare the physical top and edge shape. Report the extra slice time.

guidance: For concentric steps on a dome, compare thinner layers near the shallow top curve.
In Studio, select the object, open Variable Layer Height and use Adaptive. Review the result before slicing.
The MCP can apply an explicit local layer_heights profile. It does not generate the GUI Adaptive profile automatically.
Keep other regions coarser only when their geometry permits it. Compare actual time estimates.
scope_limits: Read catalog scopes and the actual nozzle profile before an edit.
capability_limits: P1S and other Bambu printers use their installed nozzle limits. Adaptive height is not an ironing setting.
Organic tree supports do not support variable layer height in the documented workflow.
Multicolor objects need compatible layer profiles for a shared prime tower. Review support and prime-tower preview.
Local refinement can save time versus uniformly fine layers, but it can take longer than the coarse baseline.
acceptance_checks: Inspect dome steps and transitions on a physical specimen.
Check emitted layer heights, supports and the measured time tradeoff.

categories.label: Supported surfaces
observation_needed: Identify the support-contact face and distinguish scarring from wall, seam or material defects.
Confirm support accessibility and any actual interface material.

guidance: Consider orientation and support paint before interface changes.
Compare support gap, interface layers or spacing on a representative contact specimen.
Consider another interface material only after hardware and material compatibility are confirmed.
scope_limits: These support-interface settings are project-only. Use existing support paint for face selection.
capability_limits: Zero-gap foreign-material recipes do not transfer to same-material PETG supports.
Dual-nozzle comparison times do not transfer to single-nozzle or AMS systems.
The server cannot simulate support removal or verify material compatibility.

The cited Bambu mutual-support procedure covers named PLA Basic and PETG Basic/HF products. It does not certify Matte, Silk, filled, translucent or third-party variants. Other combinations require their own evidence.
acceptance_checks: Check actual supported regions and material assignments.
Compare removal effort, scarring, dimensions and adhesion after a physical print.

guidance: On confirmed multi-nozzle hardware such as X2D, compare model material on its supported nozzle with a compatible support interface on another nozzle.
Verify the exact interface product and auxiliary nozzle restrictions before assignment.
support_filament and support_interface_filament select filament identities, not physical nozzle IDs. Confirm the separate nozzle mapping in Studio.
P1S has one nozzle. Compare same-material support settings first, or a compatible material-change interface when the actual feeder and both materials permit it.
Ordinary soft TPU does not gain automatic material changes from a top-mounted manual spool.
Compare an interface-only candidate before full support-body replacement. Include purge, time, material and contamination costs.
scope_limits: Read catalog scopes and the actual nozzle profile before an edit.
capability_limits: A second nozzle can improve separation but does not guarantee hand removal in one piece.
Zero-gap foreign-material interfaces do not transfer to same-material supports.
The MCP does not purchase hardware or prove that a support pair preserves model layer strength.
acceptance_checks: Compare a supported underside specimen with the baseline.
Record removal effort, scars, residue and layer adhesion separately.

categories.label: Dimensional fit
observation_needed: Identify the measured error, target tolerance and whether the error affects holes, outer contours or first layers.
Confirm that binding is dimensional rather than a seam ridge or rough extrusion.

guidance: Use the same filament and process for dimensional calibration.
Positive XY hole compensation increases eligible closed-hole diameters by twice the setting.
Choose an offset from measured error, not from a generic recipe.
Inspect the existing offset before an additional correction.
scope_limits: These keys are project-only. Every eligible contour can change.
Do not promise per-thread compensation with the current catalog.
capability_limits: Hole compensation affects closed slice contours.
It does not independently repair thread pitch, axial clearance, flank geometry or seam ridges.
Global scaling can alter critical dimensions. A plain bore does not validate a thread.
acceptance_checks: Measure a matched specimen and all critical affected dimensions.
For threads, check the actual screw and full engagement on the same geometry.

categories.label: Joints and local reinforcement
observation_needed: Identify the intended load, direction, assembly cycles and any actual failure.
Separate cosmetic complaints from structural failure.

guidance: Consider local walls and infill only for an identified structural need.
Compare the joint and its surrounding load path.
Explain purpose-designed insert bores or captive nuts as CAD alternatives.
Inserts can improve repeat assembly, but do not always increase joint strength.
Ask about moving parts, hinges, mating holes, cosmetic faces and load direction before a remedy.
Do not treat a fused print-in-place joint as an infill or nominal material-strength problem. Review clearances and roof/bed geometry first.
scope_limits: These keys allow project, object, volume and height_range scopes. Existing box modifiers can define local reinforcement.
capability_limits: The server cannot create insert bores, captive-nut pockets or thread CAD.
The cited PETG insert study used another printer and M3 joints.
The infill study used another material and geometry. Its numeric results are not PETG design limits.
Geometry observations and slicer estimates do not calculate safe working loads.
acceptance_checks: Use the same boss, orientation, engagement and assembly method in the specimen.
Check repeated assembly and representative loads. Record failure mode and specimen setup.

categories.label: Fine detail and visible layer steps
observation_needed: Identify the smallest required feature and distinguish layer steps from a coarse mesh or extrusion defect.
Confirm the physical nozzle diameter, material, variant and compatible filament.

guidance: Compare a smaller layer height within the installed nozzle profile limits.
Treat a 0.2 mm nozzle as a physical hardware change with compatible machine, process and filament profiles.
Do not change nozzle_diameter alone to claim a physical nozzle swap.
The 0.8, 0.6 and 0.4 mm values in a demonstration can describe nozzle diameters. Do not copy them as layer heights.
Use 0.1 mm layers only when the actual nozzle profile permits them. No fixed value suits every nozzle or filament.
scope_limits: Read catalog scopes and the actual nozzle profile before an edit.
capability_limits: A 0.2 mm nozzle needs an exact filament compatibility check, especially with flexible, filled or abrasive formulations.
Fine layers improve vertical resolution. A smaller nozzle improves lateral detail but increases time and clog sensitivity.
Neither change restores details absent from the mesh.
acceptance_checks: Inspect a small specimen with the actual fine feature.
Compare detail, support removal and print time before a full print.

guidance: Compare thin walls and pins against the project line width. Two lines are a review threshold, not the absolute printer limit.
Check detect_thin_wall against the active wall-generator mode. It cannot restore geometry below the available extrusion resolution.
Distinguish coarse mesh facets, intentional narrow CAD steps and layer stairs on shallow tops.
Use a smoother CAD export for coarse facets. Use local variable layers for layer stairs; neither control deletes intentional CAD shelves.
Treat slenderness as a geometric heuristic. Load direction, material and physical tests still determine usable strength.
scope_limits: Read current catalog scopes and project-derived nozzle, line-width and layer-height values. No universal numerical recipe.
capability_limits: Sampled normal thickness is not the global minimum. Face-normal and scan-line probes can miss local thin regions.
An STL cannot identify whether fine angular facets represent a smooth CAD curve or intentional stop steps.
A finer layer does not universally improve adhesion, bridge quality or structural strength.
acceptance_checks: Inspect normalized settings and actual paths in the thin region.
Compare a representative feature under the actual intended load.

categories.label: Flexible filament feed and stringing
observation_needed: Confirm exact flexible product, Shore hardness and scale, nozzle, drying history and complete feed path.
Distinguish strings or bubbles from spool drag, feed resistance, buckling or missed extrusion.

guidance: Check moisture and extrusion calibration before attributing every string to feed friction.
Compare a low-resistance external path for ordinary soft TPU when the exact printer guide supports it.
A compatible top spool holder can shorten the path into the toolhead. Confirm holder fit, free spool rotation and full toolhead clearance.
Disconnect or reroute PTFE only as the exact printer and material procedure instructs. Restore the path before automatic filament changes.
For P1S, confirm its external-spool loading procedure and the exact flexible product. Do not copy X2D loading temperatures or button sequences.
Keep TPU for AMS distinct from ordinary soft TPU. Verify the exact feeder compatibility before an automatic-feed recommendation.
scope_limits: Read catalog scopes and the actual nozzle profile before an edit.
capability_limits: This MCP records setup and prepares projects. It does not disconnect tubes, install holders or load filament.
A direct feed path does not cure wet filament, every retraction defect or a worn nozzle.
An X2D or P2S holder procedure does not establish fit or clearance on every Bambu printer.
acceptance_checks: Record the exact hardware path and product.
Compare a dry, representative flexible specimen for strings, surface gaps and consistent extrusion.

categories.label: Print-in-place motion and clearances
observation_needed: Identify moving components, hinge axes, side clearance, vertical clearance and the intended first-layer contact.

guidance: Run analyze_geometry on the exact revision before slicing. Show its highlighted previews and issue IDs.
Review gaps below two project line widths in XY or two project layer heights in Z. These are requested conservative heuristics, not proven failure limits.
A gap below one line width or one layer height has a higher risk rank. A 0.5 mm gap can pass that rank and retain an advisory.
The Protolabs design table recommends 0.5 mm for FDM moving/connecting parts. Prusa gives a conditional 0.3 mm starting point. Neither certifies this printer or hinge.
BBox overlap indicates a possible interlock. Confirm motion intent, then review clearance at every nominal analysis layer.
Cut out the risky joint in CAD or manually in Studio for a short coupon. Retain both mating parts, orientation and clearance.
After slicing, inspect paths in the measured void against the geometry issue ID. A path intrusion is not proof of physical fusion.
scope_limits: Read current catalog scopes and project-derived nozzle, line-width and layer-height values. No universal numerical recipe.
capability_limits: Geometry uses deterministic scan-line probes and nominal project layers. Variable profiles, local overrides and unprobed diagonal gaps can differ.
Supports or brims inside a moving clearance can fuse the joint. Extra infill does not fix a narrow clearance.
The MCP does not cut CAD, infer intended motion, or measure actual free movement.
acceptance_checks: Use the actual screw/pin and a representative hinge coupon.
Measure motion, clearance and first-layer spread after cooling.

categories.label: Horizontal holes and pins
observation_needed: Identify hole/pin axis, bore diameter, roof shape, required fit and whether the part moves.

guidance: Review circular tunnel profiles with an axis parallel to the bed. Their upper roof becomes progressively unsupported.
Use a teardrop or diamond roof with self-supporting sides, orient the axis vertically, or finish the bore after printing.
Keep pin and socket geometry compatible when motion matters. Do not add permanent support inside an inaccessible moving joint.
Compare bridge and overhang paths at the roof Z range after slicing.
XY hole compensation acts on closed XY paths. It cannot repair the open roof of a horizontal tunnel.
scope_limits: Read current catalog scopes and project-derived nozzle, line-width and layer-height values. No universal numerical recipe.
capability_limits: Circle fits measure section profiles. X/Y and up to four facet-inferred horizontal axes can miss other oblique tunnels, partial bores or tiny teardrop tips.
A diameter and axis estimate do not determine sag or a physical fit.
A horizontal external pin needs underside support; it does not have a hollow roof.
acceptance_checks: Compare a matching bore/pin coupon and inspect roof sag.
Check the actual G-code bridge direction, span and extrusion in clearance regions.

categories.label: Bed contact and first-layer clearance
observation_needed: Identify tangent curves, bottom fillets, contact footprint and measured per-side elephant-foot expansion if available.

guidance: Review steep underside facets in the near-bed band. The heuristic band is ten layers or four line widths, whichever is larger.
Prefer a flat or chamfered base over a downward bed-facing fillet when surface quality matters.
Compare first-layer gaps with a two-sided expansion budget. Use measured per-side expansion when available.
Without that measurement, the report uses half the initial line width per side as a conservative proxy.
elefant_foot_compensation shrinks the planned contour. It does not measure real squish and does not validate a moving hinge.
scope_limits: Read current catalog scopes and project-derived nozzle, line-width and layer-height values. No universal numerical recipe.
capability_limits: Bed contact assumes world Z=0. It does not simulate adhesion, thermal curl or the effect of a textured plate.
A curved base can have a narrow footprint despite a broad bounding box.
The proxy budget is not a manufacturer formula or a measured material property.
acceptance_checks: Compare the actual first-layer footprint and cooled clearance.
Calibrate compensation for the actual plate/material and inspect brim contact.

categories.label: Bridges, overhangs and floating islands
observation_needed: Identify unsupported roof spans, their direction, overhang angle convention and any floating region.

guidance: Review unsupported ceilings and their shortest horizontal facet span. That span is a candidate direction, not a calibrated maximum bridge length.
Review section regions with no overlap on the preceding nominal layer. Generated support can provide a base after slicing.
Use orientation, self-supporting geometry or removable support before a speed/cooling experiment.
Check bridge and overhang labels, move lengths and directions after slicing, linked to the original issue IDs.
Document angle conventions. The analyzer threshold is underside tilt from horizontal; it is not every slicer overhang parameter.
scope_limits: Read current catalog scopes and project-derived nozzle, line-width and layer-height values. No universal numerical recipe.
capability_limits: Prusa and Hubs give conditional overhang guidance. Protolabs lists a 10 mm FDM bridge guideline; these are not universal Bambu limits.
max_bridge_length exists in this catalog for specific unsupported-hole behavior. It is not a certified bridge capacity.
Geometry cannot prove support removability, bridge success or first-layer bonding.
acceptance_checks: Use a bridge coupon in the actual material and orientation.
Review generated support and paths near islands and moving clearances.
